title: Multiplex queue causing intermittent tail-latency regression across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Ramos
description:
Summary: Starting 2026-03-09 we received multiple escalations and internal alerts showing a regressing tail-latency (p95/p99) and reduced tokens/sec across several models when the new multiplexing scheduler is active. Impacted environments: Hosted API, several Dedicated pools, and Private customers using the shared scheduler binary.

Observed behavior: For mid-length generations (roughly 150-600 tokens) p99 TTFT increased by ~40–120ms and sustained tokens/sec dropped by ~10–20% under high concurrency bursts. Regression surfaced after the multiplex scheduler change that batches heterogeneous requests into a single worker queue with an aging heuristic. The aging weight currently favors older requests but under certain early-exit patterns a long request holds the worker KV cache and prevents smaller quick requests from getting prefetched/processed, creating head-of-line blocking.

Scope and models: Reproduced against rw-v2-medium, open-llama-13b variants, and phi-2-test snapshots. Not isolated to a single model architecture; root cause is scheduler interaction with KV cache locking and kernel selection heuristic. Customer escalations from three accounts reported production errors and SLO breaches (logs and customer screenshots attached in links).

Initial triage and hypothesis: Team observed correlation with: (1) recent change to multiplex aging coefficient (runtime commit 7a3b2c), (2) autoscaler activity that causes frequent worker churn, and (3) cases where generation exits early (e.g., stop tokens) leading to KV cache being held longer than necessary. Hypothesis: scheduler priority + cache pinning combined to create transient long-duration locks on GPU memory, increasing serialization and hurting throughput for other streams.

Temporary mitigations deployed (scope: Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private):
- Hosted: rolled back multiplexing aging coefficient and applied per-model concurrent-stream cap (hot patch) to affected clusters (2026-03-10 22:30 UTC).
- Dedicated: patched node agent to disable multiplexing on a per-pool flag for critical pools (hot patch applied 2026-03-11 03:15 UTC).
- Private: shipped v1.22.1 patch to customers with instructions to toggle scheduler.experimental_multiplex=false; solutions engineering engaged for assisted patching.

Long-term fixes in progress:
1) Scheduler change to dynamic aging weight tied to observed token-production rate and early-exit signals (PR #4832).
2) KV cache refactor to allow preemptive cache release on early-exit and 'soft pin' semantics to avoid head-of-line blocking (design doc in links).
3) Add synthetic e2e workload tests that simulate heterogeneous multiplex bursts and autoscaler-induced worker churn.
4) Telemetry additions: per-request cache-hold-time metric, multiplex queue wait histogram, and kernel-selection fallback counter.

Rollout plan: merge and e2e test PRs to staging, deploy to a subset of hosted clusters with canary traffic (1% -> 10% -> 50%), monitor p50/p95/p99 TTFT and tokens/sec, then promote to all Hosted and Dedicated pools. Private customers will receive the patch with a compatibility flag for staged rollout.

Acceptance criteria: p99 TTFT returns to baseline within 10% of pre-regression numbers under representative RPS; tokens/sec restored to within 95% of baseline for 95% of models; telemetry confirms reduction in long cache-hold events.

Risks & trade-offs: Disabling multiplexing reduces throughput efficiency in benign workloads; per-model caps may increase unit cost. Trade-off decision (approved by SRE lead) is to prefer latency/SLO stability over throughput until long-term fix is validated.

resolution_notes: Temporary mitigations (per-model caps, per-pool toggle) applied across Hosted and Dedicated; Private customers provided patch and guidance. Canary rollout of scheduler fix shows promising reduction in cache-hold events and p99 nearing baseline. Next steps: fix remaining autoscaler race found in CI, complete Dedicated rollout, and schedule postmortem with runbook updates and new multiplex stress tests.
